Location: Pipi7íyekw / Joffre Lakes Provincial Park--Lower Joffre Lake
Checklist Comments: Wow. I could probably leave the checklist notes at that - wow - Instead I will do my usual info dump. We arrived at Joffre looking to kill some time before our survey. Niall and Emile hadn’t been here before, so I talked them into going to first lake. It’s close and nice, we can wait out the snow and see how sunset is looking. We hung around the viewing area for a while, really just killing time until the sun went down. Eventually, the snow really eased off. Really eased off, so much that we realized this survey was actually a go! Then the sky cleared up, and the mountains came out. The light became stunning, and we all felt inclined to go explore the area a little bit more in the evening glow. We had played around the water’s edge for a while, but there’s only so many pictures to take of a frozen lake. So, we wondered on. We walked back up to the fork in the path, and carried on left (South.) Right after we turned the corner, Niall yelled quietly, (loudly) “Bobcat!!” Sure enough, right there in front of us was a cat. The first thing that went through my head was some kind of doubt in the initial ID. There’s no way this is a Bobcat. But I didn’t say anything, because why wouldn’t it be a Bobcat! Emile had forgotten their camera in the car, and I had forgotten my camera back in Squamish, so we were completely un distracted by anything else. Niall on the other hand, did not forget his camera. He managed to get several lovely pictures of our large cat. Thank goodness one of us did. I was so excited, I love seeing big cats. The cat had moved off the path and into bush, giving us a little bit of time to get situated and try to get some binocular looks. It was at that time that Niall vocalized what I had been thinking, but too distracted to say. Are we sure that’s a Bobcat? Looks an awful lot like a Lynx… I immediately put my vote for Canada Lynx, that doesn’t look like any Bobcat I’ve ever seen. Ear tufts were very long, that was the main thing. The cat had looked back over at us, and begun stirring. Niall predicted that it would walk back out and over the path. This cat decided to make three people’s day. Make the wildlife encounter of three people’s year. It did exactly what Niall guessed it would, it walked back out onto the path and paused on a snowbank. It turned back and stared right through me. What an unbelievably beautiful creature. To think I might not ever see another Canada Lynx… I guess I can’t complain. How could you! It kept on moving after it had posed, carrying on East towards thicker forest. Emile ran back to the car to grab their camera. Niall and I held tight in case it made a come back. When Emile got back, we checked out its prints. So light! It barely made an impact. After a little bit of scanning, Emile had one more sighting a little later, although it was fleeting - I took a picture of Niall and Emile a little after the initial encounter, I was trying to document the day thoroughly on an old digital camera of mine. Niall is beaming like he’s gone silly. Emile has the retrained smile of someone who has tough luck with missing cat photography opportunities. After the picture, Niall let me know that that was a completely genuine smile, 100%. I have to agree. I’m grinning writing this. How could we have possibly asked for more, when everything worked out the way it did. Niall was tripping out about how every part of our day had lined up just right so that we could have a once in a lifetime encounter like that. I try not to think too much about those kinds of things, there’s no end to them. But today, I gave it some thought. That’s really something - afterwards we took a couple more pictures of the pretty mountains in the beautiful light. The snow had fully stopped, and the survey was looking good. I walked out on the frozen lake like a not smart person. I wanted a silly picture. I was feeling absolutely giddy after that sighting. I was also feeling excited about the rest of the night. You’re telling me I get to spend the next bunch of hours standing around listening for owls with some of my favourite people in the world? There’s nothing else I’d rather be doing. Thanks for being my friends both of you. Thank you for being so cool, and thank you for the opportunities to experience amazing things together
Pacific White-sided Dolphins absolutely stole the show. Amazing

Oh man, what a great outing with Niall and Claudia! During the survey this morning I managed to swindle Niall into talking Claudia into looking for some dolphins with me at Porteau, and we headed out later. Zero dolphin action when we got there, so we went for a walk. I got to see Sam and Louis at the gatehouse, it was nice to catch up with them. Louis has a week left and Emily left two weeks ago. Sam’s wedding and honeymoon went really well apparently. Louis is going on exchange in Australia, and Emily left for school apparently. I caught up to where Niall and Claudia were sitting, and we pretty much just sat there for like an hour and a half at least. I drank my tea, and we just hung out really. Somewhere along the way we got word of orca at Feather Park, so we figured we’d bide our time until they came down. After some rock skipping and a lot of me bothering Niall and Claudia we went up to the beach a bit. My HADO photos were awful today as well. Eventually after watching some HADO and seals that were hanging out in the shallows, Claudia spotted a lone orca headed South. She tried so hard to point it out, but Niall and I couldn’t spot it for the life of us. She then saw it again, and I gave up. She started doubting herself, but it turns out that one left the pack early! She was totally right! Always trust your gut I guess Claudia. Eventually after some more waiting, Niall shouted “There they are, they’re swimming around under the pier!” Which confused me so much. I couldn’t see them at all, today was not my day for spotting orca. I didn’t realize he meant a couple hundred meters past the pier, and I eventually saw males. Holy crow, I always forget how big these beasts are. They are massive! They passed by pretty much right in front of us! It was so cool. The whole time we were snapping pictures like idiots, this lovely couple was hugging and watching the moment. It made me a little sad, but in a way where I hope more good things are coming in the future. (I know they are.. right?) It also made me realize how silly and dumb I can be for getting excited about photos. Here I am, trying to get a shot of these magnificent creatures, while these pure folk are embracing and taking in the moment. It really put things into perspective! I kind of laid back on the pictures after that, and tried to appreciate it. Eventually the orcas dove under, and didn’t resurface! They just have been under for minutes, because they eventually surfaced wayyyy down by the point with the grey square thing! They all came up around two kayakers, who must have had the show of their lives! It was really nice to see all that with Niall and Claudia, especially after we waited so long. My secret? It didn’t matter to me if we saw them or not. I was just glad to have some company today at the beach on a gorgeous day. In hindsight, the orcas really did become the highlight of the day though. After we watched them swim into the sunset, (literally) the nice couple approached us. They asked if we had any photos they could etransfer us for, as they were too busy taking in the moment! I almost fell over! It made me chuckle on the inside, but I am glad that they were really genuinely appreciating it all and taking it in. Apparently they just stopped here on a fluke, it was her first time seeing orcas! I guess that’s why they wanted to have a reminder of the moment. I believe Niall has the dude’s contact info. What a great day they must have had! Anyways, now that the orcas are headed out, it’s fine for some ice cream! I wonder if the place in Britannia has any vegan gluten free ice cream… lol. My hopes are not high! I waved goodbye to Louis at the gatehouse on my way out. And then we set off! What an amazing way to spend a sunny day! Beach time with good company, and some gorgeous creatures. I think I’ll remember this more than the homework I ‘should’ have been doing :)

Checklist Comments: A fantastic morning walk with Niall in the Estuary - wasn’t quite sure what to expect this morning, but it turned out to be an amazing way to spend most of the day - great lighting, and fantastic weather. Big long list today, they kind of just kept coming! Started out solid with EUWI right off the bat and some other good ducks. Made our way over to the Central Channel - I was quite excited to sit down and eat my enchiladas - when we got there, we met Mel from the NS board! They seemed very nice. When lunch was finished, we walked up to Lesley Headbanger Trail - decided to check it out and see how the trail condition is. Rough, the trail is rough. Bridge is still falling apart, super sketchy. Walk was nice on the trail! Niall found a ton of STJA, and he kept sorting thought them looking for owls or what not. Eventually, Niall found a blob that looked owlish. Tiny owl, but we couldn’t see it without thermonocular. Eventually after some heavy focusing Niall managed to get a picture of the bird’s back. Looked like a NOPO. After a bit more looking, we got confirmation. Hurray! Niall’s lifer NOPO! And he found it with his fancy toy! Such a cool moment to be around for. The bird eventually re positioned itself enough that we got a bit of a better view of it. It was still so buried though, I didn’t even bother telling Breanna (at first) because there was no world where anyone was finding this thing without a thermonocular and big boots - the trek off the Lesley Headbanger trail was a bit hectic, I even had a close call slip that Niall saw! We walked down the track and bumped into Breanna again, so I was able to tell her about NOPO. She wasn’t bothered, which was good. Niall and I loved downtown direction so I could show him Tiffany’s GCSP spot. No luck when we got there, which was a bit surprising. I’ve had lots of luck there recently, so who knows. We were looking for a WTSP reported by MC1, so this seemed like a possible spot it could show up. No dice, so we kept moving. Niall wanted coffee, so we stopped at fox and oak. I was still pretty hungry after lunch, and I folded. I bought the vegan gluten free “rotating cookie” - it was tasty, also expensive. This might be the first bird walk I’ve done where we stopped to buy stuff mid walk. Afterwards we headed West and South through downtown to the WCSP spot from last count opposite the library - eventually a few WCSP and HOFI made themselves visible,  which was a nice consolation prize. We carried on South and I blew Niall’s mind, he got super disoriented with where we were. Said he had never been to this spot before! We walked through the CAPU land there and towards Third ave. Walking down terminal road I flushed a BEKI who was perching somewhere out of sight - sorry! - we circled back after it chose a nice spot, and got some pics of it in the nice light. What a nice way to finish the walk! BEKI was so cooperative it was amazing, and such a sweetheart as well! When we got back to the tracks we took a peek for any new birds for the list, and Niall picked up DCCO. It was a good list, an amazing walk, and an absolutely fantastic day with a friend. Can you believe we picked up two CANG the whole time? Crazy! Anyways, a nice way to spend a nice day. Thanks Niall!

Location: Skwelwil'em Squamish River Estuary -- East (of central channel)
Skwelwil'em Squamish River Estuary -- East (of central channel)
Checklist Comments: Morning walk by myself and then with Niall and Claudia, then with Chris! What a fantastic morning bird. I got to the Estuary a bit before I was supposed to meet Niall and Claudia so I could go to the spot on the tracks early. Well, I didn’t realize I was at the wrong spot. Oh well! Ended up being the right call for ducks, picked up my FOY GADW and some RNDU. Tide was wayyyy in, so that was pretty cool. Eventually after some looking and some standing around, Niall let me know I was at the wrong spot. Gah! Now I’m running the length of the Estuary. Well, I got there and I hadn’t missed all that much it seems. We were hoping to get the cool RWBL breath in the morning shots. The conditions were pretty solid, but we didn’t have much for takers. One bird eventually dropped down onto the cattails and gave us some brief chances at a pic or two. I blew them, I think Niall and Claudia might have gotten lucky. We watched a heron for a bit, then had quite the surprise. Niall yelled out something like, “big weird bird” I don’t quite remember. I was looking the wrong way, and turned around to find the bird he was referring to. Oh wow, that’s a very weird bird. He called it out as a PEFA, and I can see why. However, I thought about something I didn’t want to say. I think the first thing I said was something along the lines of “that’s a very white PEFA”. And it was, it was by far the lightest falcon I’ve ever seen. Basically white on top and white underwear with a dark face mark like a PEFA. Everything else on the bird looked very good for another falcon. Niall and Claudia got some pictures, while I obviously didn’t do that. I opted to get a video of flying behaviour, because it seemed super erratic. I always think of PEFA as very methodic and intentional, but I guess I usually see them hunting. Niall said it had stooped right before I turned around, so there’s that. We talked about ID, then Claudia said what I had been thinking, probably what we were all thinking. Well, it could be. That would be unlikely though. To say the least. More research is required, I will leave it at that. Our excited chatting was interrupted by a RWBL dropping down on to a cattail and giving us a shout or two. I actually managed to get a picture, I wonder how Niall and Claudia did! I’m pretty happy with what I got. After the sun heated everything up, we moved out. Nice and warm here. We walked over to the tracks and headed down, looking for bluebirds and anything else. We encountered a song I hadn’t heard before, so I got stopped in my tracks. Eventually it clicked that it was a FOSP singing! Wow, that’s a first for me. Super cool! We hung with it for a while, then moved to carry on. We got stopped at Hawk Alley, and watched the finch show for ages. Such a good day for RECR PISI PUFI. Really some amazing views! Then we saw a familiar figure, it’s Chris! He made his way over, and then Niall picked out a TRES! Oh, FOY! It was a good day for FOY birds! It was around then I got very nervous, as Niall and Claudia started chatting about setting off! Guys, how am I supposed to see birds without you???? Eventually they headed back, Niall was cold. Fair enough, the wind had seriously picked up and the temp had surely gone down a degree or two. I still needed a couple super easy birds to make my checklist hit 40 species, so I trucked on with Chris. Well, it was cold. And not a whole lot was going down. Some SBIG wayyyy out there and some COGO as well. Well I need one more. Well I haven’t seen an eagle today. Well I guess I’ll have to settle for a pigeon in town. Well, Chris and I started heading back up the tracks. We were past Hawk Alley when my senses kicked in and I turned around. BOOM! Huge BAEA soaring right above us! Now that’s how you get a 40th bird of the day! What a show stopper, that was incredible. If you know me, I don’t really care about BAEA more than any other raptor so this may come as a surprise. I was clapping and cheering haha, what a sweet feeling! Chris and I headed on back and that was that! What an amazing morning walk, getting up early is the best! And to think it’s still March! It’s going to be a fruitful spring, I just know it! Thanks for the beautiful morning everyone, I’ve been looking forward to a day like this for ages!

Oh man, what a great outing with Niall and Claudia! During the survey this morning I managed to swindle Niall into talking Claudia into looking for some dolphins with me at Porteau, and we headed out later. Zero dolphin action when we got there, so we went for a walk. I got to see Sam and Louis at the gatehouse, it was nice to catch up with them. Louis has a week left and Emily left two weeks ago. Sam’s wedding and honeymoon went really well apparently. Louis is going on exchange in Australia, and Emily left for school apparently. I caught up to where Niall and Claudia were sitting, and we pretty much just sat there for like an hour and a half at least. I drank my tea, and we just hung out really. Somewhere along the way we got word of orca at Feather Park, so we figured we’d bide our time until they came down. After some rock skipping and a lot of me bothering Niall and Claudia we went up to the beach a bit. My HADO photos were awful today as well. Eventually after watching some HADO and seals that were hanging out in the shallows, Claudia spotted a lone orca headed South. She tried so hard to point it out, but Niall and I couldn’t spot it for the life of us. She then saw it again, and I gave up. She started doubting herself, but it turns out that one left the pack early! She was totally right! Always trust your gut I guess Claudia. Eventually after some more waiting, Niall shouted “There they are, they’re swimming around under the pier!” Which confused me so much. I couldn’t see them at all, today was not my day for spotting orca. I didn’t realize he meant a couple hundred meters past the pier, and I eventually saw males. Holy crow, I always forget how big these beasts are. They are massive! They passed by pretty much right in front of us! It was so cool. The whole time we were snapping pictures like idiots, this lovely couple was hugging and watching the moment. It made me a little sad, but in a way where I hope more good things are coming in the future. (I know they are.. right?) It also made me realize how silly and dumb I can be for getting excited about photos. Here I am, trying to get a shot of these magnificent creatures, while these pure folk are embracing and taking in the moment. It really put things into perspective! I kind of laid back on the pictures after that, and tried to appreciate it. Eventually the orcas dove under, and didn’t resurface! They just have been under for minutes, because they eventually surfaced wayyyy down by the point with the grey square thing! They all came up around two kayakers, who must have had the show of their lives! It was really nice to see all that with Niall and Claudia, especially after we waited so long. My secret? It didn’t matter to me if we saw them or not. I was just glad to have some company today at the beach on a gorgeous day. In hindsight, the orcas really did become the highlight of the day though. After we watched them swim into the sunset, (literally) the nice couple approached us. They asked if we had any photos they could etransfer us for, as they were too busy taking in the moment! I almost fell over! It made me chuckle on the inside, but I am glad that they were really genuinely appreciating it all and taking it in. Apparently they just stopped here on a fluke, it was her first time seeing orcas! I guess that’s why they wanted to have a reminder of the moment. I believe Niall has the dude’s contact info. What a great day they must have had! Anyways, now that the orcas are headed out, it’s fine for some ice cream! I wonder if the place in Britannia has any vegan gluten free ice cream… lol. My hopes are not high! I waved goodbye to Louis at the gatehouse on my way out. And then we set off! What an amazing way to spend a sunny day! Beach time with good company, and some gorgeous creatures. I think I’ll remember this more than the homework I ‘should’ have been doing :)

Checklist Comments: A fantastic morning walk with Niall in the Estuary - wasn’t quite sure what to expect this morning, but it turned out to be an amazing way to spend most of the day - great lighting, and fantastic weather. Big long list today, they kind of just kept coming! Started out solid with EUWI right off the bat and some other good ducks. Made our way over to the Central Channel - I was quite excited to sit down and eat my enchiladas - when we got there, we met Mel from the NS board! They seemed very nice. When lunch was finished, we walked up to Lesley Headbanger Trail - decided to check it out and see how the trail condition is. Rough, the trail is rough. Bridge is still falling apart, super sketchy. Walk was nice on the trail! Niall found a ton of STJA, and he kept sorting thought them looking for owls or what not. Eventually, Niall found a blob that looked owlish. Tiny owl, but we couldn’t see it without thermonocular. Eventually after some heavy focusing Niall managed to get a picture of the bird’s back. Looked like a NOPO. After a bit more looking, we got confirmation. Hurray! Niall’s lifer NOPO! And he found it with his fancy toy! Such a cool moment to be around for. The bird eventually re positioned itself enough that we got a bit of a better view of it. It was still so buried though, I didn’t even bother telling Breanna (at first) because there was no world where anyone was finding this thing without a thermonocular and big boots - the trek off the Lesley Headbanger trail was a bit hectic, I even had a close call slip that Niall saw! We walked down the track and bumped into Breanna again, so I was able to tell her about NOPO. She wasn’t bothered, which was good. Niall and I loved downtown direction so I could show him Tiffany’s GCSP spot. No luck when we got there, which was a bit surprising. I’ve had lots of luck there recently, so who knows. We were looking for a WTSP reported by MC1, so this seemed like a possible spot it could show up. No dice, so we kept moving. Niall wanted coffee, so we stopped at fox and oak. I was still pretty hungry after lunch, and I folded. I bought the vegan gluten free “rotating cookie” - it was tasty, also expensive. This might be the first bird walk I’ve done where we stopped to buy stuff mid walk. Afterwards we headed West and South through downtown to the WCSP spot from last count opposite the library - eventually a few WCSP and HOFI made themselves visible,  which was a nice consolation prize. We carried on South and I blew Niall’s mind, he got super disoriented with where we were. Said he had never been to this spot before! We walked through the CAPU land there and towards Third ave. Walking down terminal road I flushed a BEKI who was perching somewhere out of sight - sorry! - we circled back after it chose a nice spot, and got some pics of it in the nice light. What a nice way to finish the walk! BEKI was so cooperative it was amazing, and such a sweetheart as well! When we got back to the tracks we took a peek for any new birds for the list, and Niall picked up DCCO. It was a good list, an amazing walk, and an absolutely fantastic day with a friend. Can you believe we picked up two CANG the whole time? Crazy! Anyways, a nice way to spend a nice day. Thanks Niall!

We set off and caught up headed towards the tracks. We made our way down the tracks to the Bridge Pond and bumped into Chris Murrell. It was nice to see him, although I think our chatty crew might have been a bit much. It was definitely nice and quiet before we showed up. Chris found the SAPH rather quickly, and we all got our looks in. Lifer for Emile, which is always exciting! We kind of just hung around chatting about the Bird Team and other things in the warming sun. Such a treat, especially in March. This month often feels kind of dreary, so having some in your face beautiful weather was much appreciated. We hung out with the Phoebe for a while, eventually Claudia had to take off to call her Mom. Happy birthday Mrs. Cridge. Niall opted to stay with the squad, and we soaked in some more flycatcher time. Brian Aikens came around as well, so we got to chatting with him for a while also! Eventually Emile had to run off to work, so we said some quick byes. It sounds like their new job is going much better than their last one, so good news there. I’m not sure when, but after some more SAPH viewing Chris and Brian took off, and I didn’t get to say bye! Eventually Darcy showed up, so Niall and I kicked it with him for a bit until he had to run and go do something. We watched the SAPH survive a near COHA encounter! Then we walked up the tracks with Darcy. We managed to get him his lifer PUFI, so that was cool. Niall and I were already walking up the tracks, so we figured we might as well do a Nature Trust survey while we were at it. And why not? So we did! Today Niall kept a list, oh my! Survey was good, nothing all that crazy but that’s okay. Finally had a chat with the lady in the bird feeder house, she seems lovely. We carried on down and finished up the loop. That was about it, a very chill beautiful morning and early afternoon. Pretty much the best way to spend a day like this! I’m very grateful for the nice weather, and the people I have to share it with

Location: Skwelwil'em Squamish River Estuary -- East (of central channel)
Checklist Comments: Morning walk by myself and then with Niall and Claudia, then with Chris! What a fantastic morning bird. I got to the Estuary a bit before I was supposed to meet Niall and Claudia so I could go to the spot on the tracks early. Well, I didn’t realize I was at the wrong spot. Oh well! Ended up being the right call for ducks, picked up my FOY GADW and some RNDU. Tide was wayyyy in, so that was pretty cool. Eventually after some looking and some standing around, Niall let me know I was at the wrong spot. Gah! Now I’m running the length of the Estuary. Well, I got there and I hadn’t missed all that much it seems. We were hoping to get the cool RWBL breath in the morning shots. The conditions were pretty solid, but we didn’t have much for takers. One bird eventually dropped down onto the cattails and gave us some brief chances at a pic or two. I blew them, I think Niall and Claudia might have gotten lucky. We watched a heron for a bit, then had quite the surprise. Niall yelled out something like, “big weird bird” I don’t quite remember. I was looking the wrong way, and turned around to find the bird he was referring to. Oh wow, that’s a very weird bird. He called it out as a PEFA, and I can see why. However, I thought about something I didn’t want to say. I think the first thing I said was something along the lines of “that’s a very white PEFA”. And it was, it was by far the lightest falcon I’ve ever seen. Basically white on top and white underwear with a dark face mark like a PEFA. Everything else on the bird looked very good for another falcon. Niall and Claudia got some pictures, while I obviously didn’t do that. I opted to get a video of flying behaviour, because it seemed super erratic. I always think of PEFA as very methodic and intentional, but I guess I usually see them hunting. Niall said it had stooped right before I turned around, so there’s that. We talked about ID, then Claudia said what I had been thinking, probably what we were all thinking. Well, it could be. That would be unlikely though. To say the least. More research is required, I will leave it at that. Our excited chatting was interrupted by a RWBL dropping down on to a cattail and giving us a shout or two. I actually managed to get a picture, I wonder how Niall and Claudia did! I’m pretty happy with what I got. After the sun heated everything up, we moved out. Nice and warm here. We walked over to the tracks and headed down, looking for bluebirds and anything else. We encountered a song I hadn’t heard before, so I got stopped in my tracks. Eventually it clicked that it was a FOSP singing! Wow, that’s a first for me. Super cool! We hung with it for a while, then moved to carry on. We got stopped at Hawk Alley, and watched the finch show for ages. Such a good day for RECR PISI PUFI. Really some amazing views! Then we saw a familiar figure, it’s Chris! He made his way over, and then Niall picked out a TRES! Oh, FOY! It was a good day for FOY birds! It was around then I got very nervous, as Niall and Claudia started chatting about setting off! Guys, how am I supposed to see birds without you???? Eventually they headed back, Niall was cold. Fair enough, the wind had seriously picked up and the temp had surely gone down a degree or two. I still needed a couple super easy birds to make my checklist hit 40 species, so I trucked on with Chris. Well, it was cold. And not a whole lot was going down. Some SBIG wayyyy out there and some COGO as well. Well I need one more. Well I haven’t seen an eagle today. Well I guess I’ll have to settle for a pigeon in town. Well, Chris and I started heading back up the tracks. We were past Hawk Alley when my senses kicked in and I turned around. BOOM! Huge BAEA soaring right above us! Now that’s how you get a 40th bird of the day! What a show stopper, that was incredible. If you know me, I don’t really care about BAEA more than any other raptor so this may come as a surprise. I was clapping and cheering haha, what a sweet feeling! Chris and I headed on back and that was that! What an amazing morning walk, getting up early is the best! And to think it’s still March! It’s going to be a fruitful spring, I just know it! Thanks for the beautiful morning everyone, I’ve been looking forward to a day like this for ages!

Checklist Comments: Evening walk with Niall and Claudia - thanks for the walk you both. We talked business three times, I had to ask Niall a couple questions and had a few for Claudia as well! We meandered down the tracks and stood around at the usual spot. Then I got sleepy so I laid down. I was on the tracks and Claudia told me a train was coming. Well she was right wether she knew it or not. Maybe 5 - 10 minutes later a silent train backed up towards us. It was maybe 85 m away from us when either Niall or Claudia yelped and got off the tracks. That was not my wisest moment. It’s a good thing I don’t lie down on the tracks when I’m alone I guess. The worker riding the last (first approaching) car gave me a wave and that was it. I waved. Best interaction I’ve had with the railway workers in a while! Now I hadn’t brought my camera with me for some reason, and that was not smart. It was a walk of poor decisions maybe. Anyways, the locomotive was a lovely Kansas City Southern, which I’ve never seen in Squamish before! And the light was so beautiful, and the sky was beautiful, and the everything was perfect. And I didn’t have my camera ;( Oh well, I took a ton of videos, maybe I’ll throw them up in a new YouTube video. Collectable Videos 9 could be in the cards… probably not. Who knows though. Maybe a new series. Anyways, we hung around a while and eventually picked up SAPH on the far side of the BP. That was nice. When the train came back and then reversed towards the tracks once again, Niall took a picture of me in front of the locomotive! It was at my request, I didn’t want to miss the moment! I also tried taking a picture with Niall’s camera, but I’m really no good at it. In general too. We walked back up the tracks logsort bound. Darcy was about and told us about his awesome otter encounter from the other day. Cool! We finished chatting and walked up to the switchbox. We stood standing on the rail for a bit, I was having a good go. We walked out to the logsort, and that was that! Thanks for the walk both of you! Lovely day outside with friends… that certainly beats studying

Checklist Comments: Walk drive combo but mostly walk with Niall - this road is in a constant state of disrepair - we did some awesome birding for like five minutes before we got distracted by the even more awesome low tide - let’s get going on a walk to that island - and so they did, even if it was not a great idea. We had a whole lot of fun walking towards the island. Well, we hit a point where we were no longer certain we would be able to outrun the rising tide on the way back. Sooo we bailed, but not before getting all the coolest pictures. It’s real neat how the river spills over into the mudflats here. Didn’t see any herring, but I think that’s on us. Buffleheads sure did though, there was quite a bit of action from them. I had fun taking videos for a future YouTube video or something. I dunno I’m having fun making them again. Plus it was unbelievably beautiful. Niall thought he saw a fossil of some sorts! We walked along the beach and saw a super cool stone fly! Nice spot Niall! Eventually the low water table mud flat got the better of me and I had a sinkhole encounter. My own damn fault I suppose. Got some sand in the boot. Got some sand everywhere. Oh well, I’m getting better with sand. It doesn’t bother me nearly as much as it used to, maybe I’m growing up or something. Maybe. We made our way back and hit a quick Chelem trail loop. I say quick, but we dilly daddled like crazy. No rush, nothing to do, nothing but a sunny day. The wind had died down, so it was just nice. What an unbelievably beautiful part of the world we live in. I don’t even quite remember what Niall and I chatted about, but I remember being very happy and content. It’s nice feeling that way. Eventually we got up and moving to finish the loop we had barely started. We were just chilling by the PUMA boxes for that whole time. We chilled out at the Bobcat bench, but nothing. We saw two cool eagles in a tree and then we headed back down Spit road. All the way back to the car. And then I realized I didn’t take a single sign picture for Claudia and the Bird Team! Gaahhhhhh, I was just there! So I ran a quick loop while Niall warmed up Chris Dale’s bench. I got my sign pictures, then we had a nice long sit with Chris. It usually feels a little impostery for me to sit there, but it felt like the only place I should be at that moment. It was very nice. Niall shared with me that he was able to give away some of those VARC ID courses. Very cool, and very deserving recipients. We sat for a while and talked. Talked about nothing and everything. Then we headed out. I got cold! And Niall had cheap food to buy. So we headed out. We slow cruised back, and Niall let me hop out for one more sign pic. Then he dropped me at Fred. Thanks for the amazing 10/10 day buddy. I’ll remember this one! After he took off, I hung out with the waterfall for a bit. The river was really high, so I wanted to take it all in. It was cool seeing the culverts getting some real action! Anyways, I want to go skate! What an amazing unbelievable fantastic day. You just can’t beat a good day. Thanks for the day everyone

Checklist Comments: Amazing walk in the Estuary with Ella, Niall, and Tiffany! (And briefly Marcia) Ella picked out an Osprey while we were all on the tracks! It was a great moment to see this fairly terrestrial raptor soaring into the sky! As we all expected, the quest for the Yellowlegs started slow, but picked up after an hour or so when we got him! Second of Niall’s three lifers of the day! The first was him photographing what was likely my mystery peep from last week, which I assumed was LESA based on a few field marks - I left the bird in peep sp, but it feels good to have a pretty solid idea of what this bird was. Moving on to the best stop of the day, by the pothole road, we waited around with a YRWA pocket hoping to pick up some.. I’m not really sure! We were kind of just waiting around and appreciating the Warbler pocket when.. suddenly I picked up a Myrtle Warbler! Always feels good to land a mix of YRWA! And then shortly after, the bird I was hoping for all day.. Black-throated Gray Warbler! Singing at first! Got a few recordings, but missed good views.. it seems everyone else got a good look though! So cool to be reunited with my favourite Warbler! Then Tiffany picked out an OCWA! What a crazy pocket this early in migration! Such an amazing day.. on the way back we picked out a MOBL female, who very well might be the last one I see for this season.. we will see! Thanks for the great walk everyone!

Location: Skwelwil'em Squamish River Estuary -- East (of central channel)
Checklist Comments: A fantastic morning walk with Niall in the Estuary - wasn’t quite sure what to expect this morning, but it turned out to be an amazing way to spend most of the day - great lighting, and fantastic weather. Big long list today, they kind of just kept coming! Started out solid with EUWI right off the bat and some other good ducks. Made our way over to the Central Channel - I was quite excited to sit down and eat my enchiladas - when we got there, we met Mel from the NS board! They seemed very nice. When lunch was finished, we walked up to Lesley Headbanger Trail - decided to check it out and see how the trail condition is. Rough, the trail is rough. Bridge is still falling apart, super sketchy. Walk was nice on the trail! Niall found a ton of STJA, and he kept sorting thought them looking for owls or what not. Eventually, Niall found a blob that looked owlish. Tiny owl, but we couldn’t see it without thermonocular. Eventually after some heavy focusing Niall managed to get a picture of the bird’s back. Looked like a NOPO. After a bit more looking, we got confirmation. Hurray! Niall’s lifer NOPO! And he found it with his fancy toy! Such a cool moment to be around for. The bird eventually re positioned itself enough that we got a bit of a better view of it. It was still so buried though, I didn’t even bother telling Breanna (at first) because there was no world where anyone was finding this thing without a thermonocular and big boots - the trek off the Lesley Headbanger trail was a bit hectic, I even had a close call slip that Niall saw! We walked down the track and bumped into Breanna again, so I was able to tell her about NOPO. She wasn’t bothered, which was good. Niall and I loved downtown direction so I could show him Tiffany’s GCSP spot. No luck when we got there, which was a bit surprising. I’ve had lots of luck there recently, so who knows. We were looking for a WTSP reported by MC1, so this seemed like a possible spot it could show up. No dice, so we kept moving. Niall wanted coffee, so we stopped at fox and oak. I was still pretty hungry after lunch, and I folded. I bought the vegan gluten free “rotating cookie” - it was tasty, also expensive. This might be the first bird walk I’ve done where we stopped to buy stuff mid walk. Afterwards we headed West and South through downtown to the WCSP spot from last count opposite the library - eventually a few WCSP and HOFI made themselves visible,  which was a nice consolation prize. We carried on South and I blew Niall’s mind, he got super disoriented with where we were. Said he had never been to this spot before! We walked through the CAPU land there and towards Third ave. Walking down terminal road I flushed a BEKI who was perching somewhere out of sight - sorry! - we circled back after it chose a nice spot, and got some pics of it in the nice light. What a nice way to finish the walk! BEKI was so cooperative it was amazing, and such a sweetheart as well! When we got back to the tracks we took a peek for any new birds for the list, and Niall picked up DCCO. It was a good list, an amazing walk, and an absolutely fantastic day with a friend. Can you believe we picked up two CANG the whole time? Crazy! Anyways, a nice way to spend a nice day. Thanks Niall!

Location: Skwelwil'em Squamish River Estuary -- East (of central channel)
Skwelwil'em Squamish River Estuary -- East (of central channel)
Checklist Comments: Morning walk by myself and then with Niall and Claudia, then with Chris! What a fantastic morning bird. I got to the Estuary a bit before I was supposed to meet Niall and Claudia so I could go to the spot on the tracks early. Well, I didn’t realize I was at the wrong spot. Oh well! Ended up being the right call for ducks, picked up my FOY GADW and some RNDU. Tide was wayyyy in, so that was pretty cool. Eventually after some looking and some standing around, Niall let me know I was at the wrong spot. Gah! Now I’m running the length of the Estuary. Well, I got there and I hadn’t missed all that much it seems. We were hoping to get the cool RWBL breath in the morning shots. The conditions were pretty solid, but we didn’t have much for takers. One bird eventually dropped down onto the cattails and gave us some brief chances at a pic or two. I blew them, I think Niall and Claudia might have gotten lucky. We watched a heron for a bit, then had quite the surprise. Niall yelled out something like, “big weird bird” I don’t quite remember. I was looking the wrong way, and turned around to find the bird he was referring to. Oh wow, that’s a very weird bird. He called it out as a PEFA, and I can see why. However, I thought about something I didn’t want to say. I think the first thing I said was something along the lines of “that’s a very white PEFA”. And it was, it was by far the lightest falcon I’ve ever seen. Basically white on top and white underwear with a dark face mark like a PEFA. Everything else on the bird looked very good for another falcon. Niall and Claudia got some pictures, while I obviously didn’t do that. I opted to get a video of flying behaviour, because it seemed super erratic. I always think of PEFA as very methodic and intentional, but I guess I usually see them hunting. Niall said it had stooped right before I turned around, so there’s that. We talked about ID, then Claudia said what I had been thinking, probably what we were all thinking. Well, it could be. That would be unlikely though. To say the least. More research is required, I will leave it at that. Our excited chatting was interrupted by a RWBL dropping down on to a cattail and giving us a shout or two. I actually managed to get a picture, I wonder how Niall and Claudia did! I’m pretty happy with what I got. After the sun heated everything up, we moved out. Nice and warm here. We walked over to the tracks and headed down, looking for bluebirds and anything else. We encountered a song I hadn’t heard before, so I got stopped in my tracks. Eventually it clicked that it was a FOSP singing! Wow, that’s a first for me. Super cool! We hung with it for a while, then moved to carry on. We got stopped at Hawk Alley, and watched the finch show for ages. Such a good day for RECR PISI PUFI. Really some amazing views! Then we saw a familiar figure, it’s Chris! He made his way over, and then Niall picked out a TRES! Oh, FOY! It was a good day for FOY birds! It was around then I got very nervous, as Niall and Claudia started chatting about setting off! Guys, how am I supposed to see birds without you???? Eventually they headed back, Niall was cold. Fair enough, the wind had seriously picked up and the temp had surely gone down a degree or two. I still needed a couple super easy birds to make my checklist hit 40 species, so I trucked on with Chris. Well, it was cold. And not a whole lot was going down. Some SBIG wayyyy out there and some COGO as well. Well I need one more. Well I haven’t seen an eagle today. Well I guess I’ll have to settle for a pigeon in town. Well, Chris and I started heading back up the tracks. We were past Hawk Alley when my senses kicked in and I turned around. BOOM! Huge BAEA soaring right above us! Now that’s how you get a 40th bird of the day! What a show stopper, that was incredible. If you know me, I don’t really care about BAEA more than any other raptor so this may come as a surprise. I was clapping and cheering haha, what a sweet feeling! Chris and I headed on back and that was that! What an amazing morning walk, getting up early is the best! And to think it’s still March! It’s going to be a fruitful spring, I just know it! Thanks for the beautiful morning everyone, I’ve been looking forward to a day like this for ages!

Evening dyke walk with Niall - first time doing the dyke loop with Niall - incredibly slow - dropped down and did the bit by the swimming hole - we made our way over to beaver pond and Niall spotted a beaver - amazing - then we headed back

Evening walk with Niall on the dyke loop - I’m grateful to have a friend I can show places. Although this loop isn’t technically new to Niall, it kind of feels like it might be. I’ve been here a few times with him, each time the birds have been less active than usual. Today was pretty good! The point of our walk was to look for the beavers in the beaver pond. Well we didn’t rush down there, but were ultimately successful. We stopped and looked for the NRWS from last year, but didn’t see any activity at all. We carried on in the woods and popped out on the bridge trail. We saw Breanna, who let us know that she had just had a beaver slap its tail. We hung around, and Niall spotted one making its way through the water. It had white fluffs stuck to its head! The beaver did a lap, and posted up on a bank. It gave great looks and mowed down on a large branch. It did a lap, and returned to do the same thing. Eventually, it took the cedar branch and started dragging it across the pond. The thing was so big that the beaver could only pull it in a jerking bobbing motion. Like two steps forward, one step back. What a crazy thing. It was a blast to watch. Niall and I made our way back up, and that was that. Thanks for the walk buddy!

Checklist Comments: Morning walk by myself and then with Niall and Claudia, then with Chris! What a fantastic morning bird. I got to the Estuary a bit before I was supposed to meet Niall and Claudia so I could go to the spot on the tracks early. Well, I didn’t realize I was at the wrong spot. Oh well! Ended up being the right call for ducks, picked up my FOY GADW and some RNDU. Tide was wayyyy in, so that was pretty cool. Eventually after some looking and some standing around, Niall let me know I was at the wrong spot. Gah! Now I’m running the length of the Estuary. Well, I got there and I hadn’t missed all that much it seems. We were hoping to get the cool RWBL breath in the morning shots. The conditions were pretty solid, but we didn’t have much for takers. One bird eventually dropped down onto the cattails and gave us some brief chances at a pic or two. I blew them, I think Niall and Claudia might have gotten lucky. We watched a heron for a bit, then had quite the surprise. Niall yelled out something like, “big weird bird” I don’t quite remember. I was looking the wrong way, and turned around to find the bird he was referring to. Oh wow, that’s a very weird bird. He called it out as a PEFA, and I can see why. However, I thought about something I didn’t want to say. I think the first thing I said was something along the lines of “that’s a very white PEFA”. And it was, it was by far the lightest falcon I’ve ever seen. Basically white on top and white underwear with a dark face mark like a PEFA. Everything else on the bird looked very good for another falcon. Niall and Claudia got some pictures, while I obviously didn’t do that. I opted to get a video of flying behaviour, because it seemed super erratic. I always think of PEFA as very methodic and intentional, but I guess I usually see them hunting. Niall said it had stooped right before I turned around, so there’s that. We talked about ID, then Claudia said what I had been thinking, probably what we were all thinking. Well, it could be. That would be unlikely though. To say the least. More research is required, I will leave it at that. Our excited chatting was interrupted by a RWBL dropping down on to a cattail and giving us a shout or two. I actually managed to get a picture, I wonder how Niall and Claudia did! I’m pretty happy with what I got. After the sun heated everything up, we moved out. Nice and warm here. We walked over to the tracks and headed down, looking for bluebirds and anything else. We encountered a song I hadn’t heard before, so I got stopped in my tracks. Eventually it clicked that it was a FOSP singing! Wow, that’s a first for me. Super cool! We hung with it for a while, then moved to carry on. We got stopped at Hawk Alley, and watched the finch show for ages. Such a good day for RECR PISI PUFI. Really some amazing views! Then we saw a familiar figure, it’s Chris! He made his way over, and then Niall picked out a TRES! Oh, FOY! It was a good day for FOY birds! It was around then I got very nervous, as Niall and Claudia started chatting about setting off! Guys, how am I supposed to see birds without you???? Eventually they headed back, Niall was cold. Fair enough, the wind had seriously picked up and the temp had surely gone down a degree or two. I still needed a couple super easy birds to make my checklist hit 40 species, so I trucked on with Chris. Well, it was cold. And not a whole lot was going down. Some SBIG wayyyy out there and some COGO as well. Well I need one more. Well I haven’t seen an eagle today. Well I guess I’ll have to settle for a pigeon in town. Well, Chris and I started heading back up the tracks. We were past Hawk Alley when my senses kicked in and I turned around. BOOM! Huge BAEA soaring right above us! Now that’s how you get a 40th bird of the day! What a show stopper, that was incredible. If you know me, I don’t really care about BAEA more than any other raptor so this may come as a surprise. I was clapping and cheering haha, what a sweet feeling! Chris and I headed on back and that was that! What an amazing morning walk, getting up early is the best! And to think it’s still March! It’s going to be a fruitful spring, I just know it! Thanks for the beautiful morning everyone, I’ve been looking forward to a day like this for ages!

Morning with the bluebirds by myself then with company. Managed to sneak out this am for a quick whirl of Feather Park, I was thrilled to see the bluebirds still hanging around the grass field. I sat and watched them, took pictures, and sat, and took pictures. And then I stood up and walked around because I was freezing. Eventually Bonnie spotted me, and we chatted for a bit. Niall showed up as well and we took some pics. Really we were just waiting for them to go back to the beach. Eventually it happened, and we walked after them. They were moving around a bunch, and… increasing in numbers? We had a solid count of twelve or thirteen earlier in the day but now… that’s how many are just in this field here… Niall did another count. Twenty one! We got it twice! So many bluebirds! We also had some meadowlarks and an adorable cackler. There was also a large, like 100 person group of student age folk who arrived on two large busses. We ended up chatting to someone from Montreal, they were on some sort of ocean science five day super speed tour. Today was Squamish and the Pacific Ocean, soon was the Maritimes and the Atlantic Ocean! Crazy! We let them on their way, and we got back to the bluebirds. Soon Emile and Niamh showed up! Hey! Niall, Emile, and I sat on a log and tried to get some good pics. I think most of my best photos were from then. It was a lot of fun taking pictures with my friends above, under, and around eachother! There were so many birds popping up and around that we stopped calling them out, and kind of just grunted and gestured. What a fantastic time. Unfortunately, I got cold. Reaaaal cold. I ended up needing to go warm my hands up, so I let Emile and Niamh go. Ella was also there, she seemed excited by the bluebirds! Anyways, Niall and I took off. Time to go to school I guess. This was definitely more fun. Great day!

Location: Skwelwil'em Squamish River Estuary -- East (of central channel)
Checklist Comments: A fantastic morning walk with Niall in the Estuary - wasn’t quite sure what to expect this morning, but it turned out to be an amazing way to spend most of the day - great lighting, and fantastic weather. Big long list today, they kind of just kept coming! Started out solid with EUWI right off the bat and some other good ducks. Made our way over to the Central Channel - I was quite excited to sit down and eat my enchiladas - when we got there, we met Mel from the NS board! They seemed very nice. When lunch was finished, we walked up to Lesley Headbanger Trail - decided to check it out and see how the trail condition is. Rough, the trail is rough. Bridge is still falling apart, super sketchy. Walk was nice on the trail! Niall found a ton of STJA, and he kept sorting thought them looking for owls or what not. Eventually, Niall found a blob that looked owlish. Tiny owl, but we couldn’t see it without thermonocular. Eventually after some heavy focusing Niall managed to get a picture of the bird’s back. Looked like a NOPO. After a bit more looking, we got confirmation. Hurray! Niall’s lifer NOPO! And he found it with his fancy toy! Such a cool moment to be around for. The bird eventually re positioned itself enough that we got a bit of a better view of it. It was still so buried though, I didn’t even bother telling Breanna (at first) because there was no world where anyone was finding this thing without a thermonocular and big boots - the trek off the Lesley Headbanger trail was a bit hectic, I even had a close call slip that Niall saw! We walked down the track and bumped into Breanna again, so I was able to tell her about NOPO. She wasn’t bothered, which was good. Niall and I loved downtown direction so I could show him Tiffany’s GCSP spot. No luck when we got there, which was a bit surprising. I’ve had lots of luck there recently, so who knows. We were looking for a WTSP reported by MC1, so this seemed like a possible spot it could show up. No dice, so we kept moving. Niall wanted coffee, so we stopped at fox and oak. I was still pretty hungry after lunch, and I folded. I bought the vegan gluten free “rotating cookie” - it was tasty, also expensive. This might be the first bird walk I’ve done where we stopped to buy stuff mid walk. Afterwards we headed West and South through downtown to the WCSP spot from last count opposite the library - eventually a few WCSP and HOFI made themselves visible,  which was a nice consolation prize. We carried on South and I blew Niall’s mind, he got super disoriented with where we were. Said he had never been to this spot before! We walked through the CAPU land there and towards Third ave. Walking down terminal road I flushed a BEKI who was perching somewhere out of sight - sorry! - we circled back after it chose a nice spot, and got some pics of it in the nice light. What a nice way to finish the walk! BEKI was so cooperative it was amazing, and such a sweetheart as well! When we got back to the tracks we took a peek for any new birds for the list, and Niall picked up DCCO. It was a good list, an amazing walk, and an absolutely fantastic day with a friend. Can you believe we picked up two CANG the whole time? Crazy! Anyways, a nice way to spend a nice day. Thanks Niall!

Checklist Comments: Goodmorning walk with a very solid crew. Met up with Niall, Claudia, and Emile by Vancouver street. Started off strong with birds calling and the sun shining. We set off and caught up headed towards the tracks. We made our way down the tracks to the Bridge Pond and bumped into Chris Murrell. It was nice to see him, although I think our chatty crew might have been a bit much. It was definitely nice and quiet before we showed up. Chris found the SAPH rather quickly, and we all got our looks in. Lifer for Emile, which is always exciting! We kind of just hung around chatting about the Bird Team and other things in the warming sun. Such a treat, especially in March. This month often feels kind of dreary, so having some in your face beautiful weather was much appreciated. We hung out with the Phoebe for a while, eventually Claudia had to take off to call her Mom. Happy birthday Mrs. Cridge. Niall opted to stay with the squad, and we soaked in some more flycatcher time. Brian Aikens came around as well, so we got to chatting with him for a while also! Eventually Emile had to run off to work, so we said some quick byes. It sounds like their new job is going much better than their last one, so good news there. I’m not sure when, but after some more SAPH viewing Chris and Brian took off, and I didn’t get to say bye! Eventually Darcy showed up, so Niall and I kicked it with him for a bit until he had to run and go do something. We watched the SAPH survive a near COHA encounter! Then we walked up the tracks with Darcy. We managed to get him his lifer PUFI, so that was cool. Niall and I were already walking up the tracks, so we figured we might as well do a Nature Trust survey while we were at it. And why not? So we did! Today Niall kept a list, oh my! Survey was good, nothing all that crazy but that’s okay. Finally had a chat with the lady in the bird feeder house, she seems lovely. We carried on down and finished up the loop. That was about it, a very chill beautiful morning and early afternoon. Pretty much the best way to spend a day like this! I’m very grateful for the nice weather, and the people I have to share it with

Location: Skwelwil'em Squamish River Estuary -- East (of central channel)
Checklist Comments: Evening walk with Niall and Claudia - thanks for the walk you both. We talked business three times, I had to ask Niall a couple questions and had a few for Claudia as well! We meandered down the tracks and stood around at the usual spot. Then I got sleepy so I laid down. I was on the tracks and Claudia told me a train was coming. Well she was right wether she knew it or not. Maybe 5 - 10 minutes later a silent train backed up towards us. It was maybe 85 m away from us when either Niall or Claudia yelped and got off the tracks. That was not my wisest moment. It’s a good thing I don’t lie down on the tracks when I’m alone I guess. The worker riding the last (first approaching) car gave me a wave and that was it. I waved. Best interaction I’ve had with the railway workers in a while! Now I hadn’t brought my camera with me for some reason, and that was not smart. It was a walk of poor decisions maybe. Anyways, the locomotive was a lovely Kansas City Southern, which I’ve never seen in Squamish before! And the light was so beautiful, and the sky was beautiful, and the everything was perfect. And I didn’t have my camera ;( Oh well, I took a ton of videos, maybe I’ll throw them up in a new YouTube video. Collectable Videos 9 could be in the cards… probably not. Who knows though. Maybe a new series. Anyways, we hung around a while and eventually picked up SAPH on the far side of the BP. That was nice. When the train came back and then reversed towards the tracks once again, Niall took a picture of me in front of the locomotive! It was at my request, I didn’t want to miss the moment! I also tried taking a picture with Niall’s camera, but I’m really no good at it. In general too. We walked back up the tracks logsort bound. Darcy was about and told us about his awesome otter encounter from the other day. Cool! We finished chatting and walked up to the switchbox. We stood standing on the rail for a bit, I was having a good go. We walked out to the logsort, and that was that! Thanks for the walk both of you! Lovely day outside with friends… that certainly beats studying

The CITE was with NSHO earlier in the day, so it was a bad sign they were nowhere to be seen. We scoped for a while, but nothing new turned up. We moved down to the logsort CC spot and scoped from there. I picked up a GRYE then kinda gave up. It was windy. Eventually I looked up for some reason, maybe for one last scope. Holy moly, that’s two big shorebirds. I found the curlew from earlier Niall! We got some extremely distant views, they were so far out there. Anyways, just fun to see them really. We kept on moving pretty quick after that. We made our way back down the tracks. We saw Bonnie waving frantically and she pointed at a beautiful AMKE. It gave amazing views, I’m excited to go through my pictures. We got some looks and then Niall went over to help her with her camera. I drove over and chatted with them. And then that was it! I was so tired I needed to go home. Long day of birding, I’m beat. Thanks for the walk Niall, I trust we will be back out tomorrow morning

Oh man, what a great outing with Niall and Claudia! During the survey this morning I managed to swindle Niall into talking Claudia into looking for some dolphins with me at Porteau, and we headed out later. Zero dolphin action when we got there, so we went for a walk. I got to see Sam and Louis at the gatehouse, it was nice to catch up with them. Louis has a week left and Emily left two weeks ago. Sam’s wedding and honeymoon went really well apparently. Louis is going on exchange in Australia, and Emily left for school apparently. I caught up to where Niall and Claudia were sitting, and we pretty much just sat there for like an hour and a half at least. I drank my tea, and we just hung out really. Somewhere along the way we got word of orca at Feather Park, so we figured we’d bide our time until they came down. After some rock skipping and a lot of me bothering Niall and Claudia we went up to the beach a bit. My HADO photos were awful today as well. Eventually after watching some HADO and seals that were hanging out in the shallows, Claudia spotted a lone orca headed South. She tried so hard to point it out, but Niall and I couldn’t spot it for the life of us. She then saw it again, and I gave up. She started doubting herself, but it turns out that one left the pack early! She was totally right! Always trust your gut I guess Claudia. Eventually after some more waiting, Niall shouted “There they are, they’re swimming around under the pier!” Which confused me so much. I couldn’t see them at all, today was not my day for spotting orca. I didn’t realize he meant a couple hundred meters past the pier, and I eventually saw males. Holy crow, I always forget how big these beasts are. They are massive! They passed by pretty much right in front of us! It was so cool. The whole time we were snapping pictures like idiots, this lovely couple was hugging and watching the moment. It made me a little sad, but in a way where I hope more good things are coming in the future. (I know they are.. right?) It also made me realize how silly and dumb I can be for getting excited about photos. Here I am, trying to get a shot of these magnificent creatures, while these pure folk are embracing and taking in the moment. It really put things into perspective! I kind of laid back on the pictures after that, and tried to appreciate it. Eventually the orcas dove under, and didn’t resurface! They just have been under for minutes, because they eventually surfaced wayyyy down by the point with the grey square thing! They all came up around two kayakers, who must have had the show of their lives! It was really nice to see all that with Niall and Claudia, especially after we waited so long. My secret? It didn’t matter to me if we saw them or not. I was just glad to have some company today at the beach on a gorgeous day. In hindsight, the orcas really did become the highlight of the day though. After we watched them swim into the sunset, (literally) the nice couple approached us. They asked if we had any photos they could etransfer us for, as they were too busy taking in the moment! I almost fell over! It made me chuckle on the inside, but I am glad that they were really genuinely appreciating it all and taking it in. Apparently they just stopped here on a fluke, it was her first time seeing orcas! I guess that’s why they wanted to have a reminder of the moment. I believe Niall has the dude’s contact info. What a great day they must have had! Anyways, now that the orcas are headed out, it’s fine for some ice cream! I wonder if the place in Britannia has any vegan gluten free ice cream… lol. My hopes are not high! I waved goodbye to Louis at the gatehouse on my way out. And then we set off! What an amazing way to spend a sunny day! Beach time with good company, and some gorgeous creatures. I think I’ll remember this more than the homework I ‘should’ have been doing :)

Checklist Comments: A fantastic morning walk with Niall in the Estuary - wasn’t quite sure what to expect this morning, but it turned out to be an amazing way to spend most of the day - great lighting, and fantastic weather. Big long list today, they kind of just kept coming! Started out solid with EUWI right off the bat and some other good ducks. Made our way over to the Central Channel - I was quite excited to sit down and eat my enchiladas - when we got there, we met Mel from the NS board! They seemed very nice. When lunch was finished, we walked up to Lesley Headbanger Trail - decided to check it out and see how the trail condition is. Rough, the trail is rough. Bridge is still falling apart, super sketchy. Walk was nice on the trail! Niall found a ton of STJA, and he kept sorting thought them looking for owls or what not. Eventually, Niall found a blob that looked owlish. Tiny owl, but we couldn’t see it without thermonocular. Eventually after some heavy focusing Niall managed to get a picture of the bird’s back. Looked like a NOPO. After a bit more looking, we got confirmation. Hurray! Niall’s lifer NOPO! And he found it with his fancy toy! Such a cool moment to be around for. The bird eventually re positioned itself enough that we got a bit of a better view of it. It was still so buried though, I didn’t even bother telling Breanna (at first) because there was no world where anyone was finding this thing without a thermonocular and big boots - the trek off the Lesley Headbanger trail was a bit hectic, I even had a close call slip that Niall saw! We walked down the track and bumped into Breanna again, so I was able to tell her about NOPO. She wasn’t bothered, which was good. Niall and I loved downtown direction so I could show him Tiffany’s GCSP spot. No luck when we got there, which was a bit surprising. I’ve had lots of luck there recently, so who knows. We were looking for a WTSP reported by MC1, so this seemed like a possible spot it could show up. No dice, so we kept moving. Niall wanted coffee, so we stopped at fox and oak. I was still pretty hungry after lunch, and I folded. I bought the vegan gluten free “rotating cookie” - it was tasty, also expensive. This might be the first bird walk I’ve done where we stopped to buy stuff mid walk. Afterwards we headed West and South through downtown to the WCSP spot from last count opposite the library - eventually a few WCSP and HOFI made themselves visible,  which was a nice consolation prize. We carried on South and I blew Niall’s mind, he got super disoriented with where we were. Said he had never been to this spot before! We walked through the CAPU land there and towards Third ave. Walking down terminal road I flushed a BEKI who was perching somewhere out of sight - sorry! - we circled back after it chose a nice spot, and got some pics of it in the nice light. What a nice way to finish the walk! BEKI was so cooperative it was amazing, and such a sweetheart as well! When we got back to the tracks we took a peek for any new birds for the list, and Niall picked up DCCO. It was a good list, an amazing walk, and an absolutely fantastic day with a friend. Can you believe we picked up two CANG the whole time? Crazy! Anyways, a nice way to spend a nice day. Thanks Niall!

Location: Skwelwil'em Squamish River Estuary -- East (of central channel)
Checklist Comments: Morning walk by myself and then with Niall and Claudia, then with Chris! What a fantastic morning bird. I got to the Estuary a bit before I was supposed to meet Niall and Claudia so I could go to the spot on the tracks early. Well, I didn’t realize I was at the wrong spot. Oh well! Ended up being the right call for ducks, picked up my FOY GADW and some RNDU. Tide was wayyyy in, so that was pretty cool. Eventually after some looking and some standing around, Niall let me know I was at the wrong spot. Gah! Now I’m running the length of the Estuary. Well, I got there and I hadn’t missed all that much it seems. We were hoping to get the cool RWBL breath in the morning shots. The conditions were pretty solid, but we didn’t have much for takers. One bird eventually dropped down onto the cattails and gave us some brief chances at a pic or two. I blew them, I think Niall and Claudia might have gotten lucky. We watched a heron for a bit, then had quite the surprise. Niall yelled out something like, “big weird bird” I don’t quite remember. I was looking the wrong way, and turned around to find the bird he was referring to. Oh wow, that’s a very weird bird. He called it out as a PEFA, and I can see why. However, I thought about something I didn’t want to say. I think the first thing I said was something along the lines of “that’s a very white PEFA”. And it was, it was by far the lightest falcon I’ve ever seen. Basically white on top and white underwear with a dark face mark like a PEFA. Everything else on the bird looked very good for another falcon. Niall and Claudia got some pictures, while I obviously didn’t do that. I opted to get a video of flying behaviour, because it seemed super erratic. I always think of PEFA as very methodic and intentional, but I guess I usually see them hunting. Niall said it had stooped right before I turned around, so there’s that. We talked about ID, then Claudia said what I had been thinking, probably what we were all thinking. Well, it could be. That would be unlikely though. To say the least. More research is required, I will leave it at that. Our excited chatting was interrupted by a RWBL dropping down on to a cattail and giving us a shout or two. I actually managed to get a picture, I wonder how Niall and Claudia did! I’m pretty happy with what I got. After the sun heated everything up, we moved out. Nice and warm here. We walked over to the tracks and headed down, looking for bluebirds and anything else. We encountered a song I hadn’t heard before, so I got stopped in my tracks. Eventually it clicked that it was a FOSP singing! Wow, that’s a first for me. Super cool! We hung with it for a while, then moved to carry on. We got stopped at Hawk Alley, and watched the finch show for ages. Such a good day for RECR PISI PUFI. Really some amazing views! Then we saw a familiar figure, it’s Chris! He made his way over, and then Niall picked out a TRES! Oh, FOY! It was a good day for FOY birds! It was around then I got very nervous, as Niall and Claudia started chatting about setting off! Guys, how am I supposed to see birds without you???? Eventually they headed back, Niall was cold. Fair enough, the wind had seriously picked up and the temp had surely gone down a degree or two. I still needed a couple super easy birds to make my checklist hit 40 species, so I trucked on with Chris. Well, it was cold. And not a whole lot was going down. Some SBIG wayyyy out there and some COGO as well. Well I need one more. Well I haven’t seen an eagle today. Well I guess I’ll have to settle for a pigeon in town. Well, Chris and I started heading back up the tracks. We were past Hawk Alley when my senses kicked in and I turned around. BOOM! Huge BAEA soaring right above us! Now that’s how you get a 40th bird of the day! What a show stopper, that was incredible. If you know me, I don’t really care about BAEA more than any other raptor so this may come as a surprise. I was clapping and cheering haha, what a sweet feeling! Chris and I headed on back and that was that! What an amazing morning walk, getting up early is the best! And to think it’s still March! It’s going to be a fruitful spring, I just know it! Thanks for the beautiful morning everyone, I’ve been looking forward to a day like this for ages!

It was maybe 85 m away from us when either Niall or Claudia yelped and got off the tracks. That was not my wisest moment. It’s a good thing I don’t lie down on the tracks when I’m alone I guess. The worker riding the last (first approaching) car gave me a wave and that was it. I waved. Best interaction I’ve had with the railway workers in a while! Now I hadn’t brought my camera with me for some reason, and that was not smart. It was a walk of poor decisions maybe. Anyways, the locomotive was a lovely Kansas City Southern, which I’ve never seen in Squamish before! And the light was so beautiful, and the sky was beautiful, and the everything was perfect. And I didn’t have my camera ;( Oh well, I took a ton of videos, maybe I’ll throw them up in a new YouTube video. Collectable Videos 9 could be in the cards… probably not. Who knows though. Maybe a new series. Anyways, we hung around a while and eventually picked up SAPH on the far side of the BP. That was nice. When the train came back and then reversed towards the tracks once again, Niall took a picture of me in front of the locomotive! It was at my request, I didn’t want to miss the moment! I also tried taking a picture with Niall’s camera, but I’m really no good at it. In general too. We walked back up the tracks logsort bound. Darcy was about and told us about his awesome otter encounter from the other day. Cool! We finished chatting and walked up to the switchbox. We stood standing on the rail for a bit, I was having a good go. We walked out to the logsort, and that was that! Thanks for the walk both of you! Lovely day outside with friends… that certainly beats studying

Checklist Comments: Walk drive combo but mostly walk with Niall - this road is in a constant state of disrepair - we did some awesome birding for like five minutes before we got distracted by the even more awesome low tide - let’s get going on a walk to that island - and so they did, even if it was not a great idea. We had a whole lot of fun walking towards the island. Well, we hit a point where we were no longer certain we would be able to outrun the rising tide on the way back. Sooo we bailed, but not before getting all the coolest pictures. It’s real neat how the river spills over into the mudflats here. Didn’t see any herring, but I think that’s on us. Buffleheads sure did though, there was quite a bit of action from them. I had fun taking videos for a future YouTube video or something. I dunno I’m having fun making them again. Plus it was unbelievably beautiful. Niall thought he saw a fossil of some sorts! We walked along the beach and saw a super cool stone fly! Nice spot Niall! Eventually the low water table mud flat got the better of me and I had a sinkhole encounter. My own damn fault I suppose. Got some sand in the boot. Got some sand everywhere. Oh well, I’m getting better with sand. It doesn’t bother me nearly as much as it used to, maybe I’m growing up or something. Maybe. We made our way back and hit a quick Chelem trail loop. I say quick, but we dilly daddled like crazy. No rush, nothing to do, nothing but a sunny day. The wind had died down, so it was just nice. What an unbelievably beautiful part of the world we live in. I don’t even quite remember what Niall and I chatted about, but I remember being very happy and content. It’s nice feeling that way. Eventually we got up and moving to finish the loop we had barely started. We were just chilling by the PUMA boxes for that whole time. We chilled out at the Bobcat bench, but nothing. We saw two cool eagles in a tree and then we headed back down Spit road. All the way back to the car. And then I realized I didn’t take a single sign picture for Claudia and the Bird Team! Gaahhhhhh, I was just there! So I ran a quick loop while Niall warmed up Chris Dale’s bench. I got my sign pictures, then we had a nice long sit with Chris. It usually feels a little impostery for me to sit there, but it felt like the only place I should be at that moment. It was very nice. Niall shared with me that he was able to give away some of those VARC ID courses. Very cool, and very deserving recipients. We sat for a while and talked. Talked about nothing and everything. Then we headed out. I got cold! And Niall had cheap food to buy. So we headed out. We slow cruised back, and Niall let me hop out for one more sign pic. Then he dropped me at Fred. Thanks for the amazing 10/10 day buddy. I’ll remember this one! After he took off, I hung out with the waterfall for a bit. The river was really high, so I wanted to take it all in. It was cool seeing the culverts getting some real action! Anyways, I want to go skate! What an amazing unbelievable fantastic day. You just can’t beat a good day. Thanks for the day everyone

Evening walk with Niall on the dyke loop - I’m grateful to have a friend I can show places. Although this loop isn’t technically new to Niall, it kind of feels like it might be. I’ve been here a few times with him, each time the birds have been less active than usual. Today was pretty good! The point of our walk was to look for the beavers in the beaver pond. Well we didn’t rush down there, but were ultimately successful. We stopped and looked for the NRWS from last year, but didn’t see any activity at all. We carried on in the woods and popped out on the bridge trail. We saw Breanna, who let us know that she had just had a beaver slap its tail. We hung around, and Niall spotted one making its way through the water. It had white fluffs stuck to its head! The beaver did a lap, and posted up on a bank. It gave great looks and mowed down on a large branch. It did a lap, and returned to do the same thing. Eventually, it took the cedar branch and started dragging it across the pond. The thing was so big that the beaver could only pull it in a jerking bobbing motion. Like two steps forward, one step back. What a crazy thing. It was a blast to watch. Niall and I made our way back up, and that was that. Thanks for the walk buddy!

Evening walk with Niall on the dyke loop - I’m grateful to have a friend I can show places. Although this loop isn’t technically new to Niall, it kind of feels like it might be. I’ve been here a few times with him, each time the birds have been less active than usual. Today was pretty good! The point of our walk was to look for the beavers in the beaver pond. Well we didn’t rush down there, but were ultimately successful. We stopped and looked for the NRWS from last year, but didn’t see any activity at all. We carried on in the woods and popped out on the bridge trail. We saw Breanna, who let us know that she had just had a beaver slap its tail. We hung around, and Niall spotted one making its way through the water. It had white fluffs stuck to its head! The beaver did a lap, and posted up on a bank. It gave great looks and mowed down on a large branch. It did a lap, and returned to do the same thing. Eventually, it took the cedar branch and started dragging it across the pond. The thing was so big that the beaver could only pull it in a jerking bobbing motion. Like two steps forward, one step back. What a crazy thing. It was a blast to watch. Niall and I made our way back up, and that was that. Thanks for the walk buddy!
